one_line: Master sculptor of the Hoysala workshops at Halebidu and Belur, 12th–13th century Karnataka.

appearance.age_look: late 30s, wiry and agile build, craftsman’s strength rather than warrior bulk
appearance.face: oval face with warm medium-brown complexion, sharp nose, high cheekbones, faint chisel nicks on the cheeks, thoughtful narrow eyes with a calm focused gaze, default expression a small, knowing half-smile of concentration
appearance.hair: thick black hair pulled back into a neat low knot at the back of the head, front kept tidy with a short center part; simple off-white cotton headband tied around the forehead to keep hair and sweat back, ends tucked in
appearance.costume: a knee-length, long-sleeved cotton tunic (angiya-style) in muted indigo blue with a subtle woven grid pattern, worn over a cream-colored cotton dhoti wrapped firmly and pleated in front, reaching the ankles; the dhoti has a narrow dark brown border; over one shoulder is a soft, light-brown cotton angavastra drape that can be shifted while he works; simple leather sandals; modest jewellery limited to a thin gold chain at the neck and a pair of small gold studs in the ears; forearms wrapped with plain off-white cloth bands to protect from stone dust, and a simple fabric belt at the waist holding small tools
appearance.signature: a long, slightly worn iron chisel with a square-section shaft and flattened cutting edge, held in his right hand, paired with a medium wooden mallet in the left, both showing years of use and stone dust

ref_desc: Ruvari Mallitamma is a late-30s Hoysala sculptor with medium-brown skin, black hair in a low knot and off-white headband, wearing an indigo tunic, cream dhoti, light-brown shoulder cloth, simple gold accents, and carrying an iron chisel and wooden mallet.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of Ruvari Mallitamma, a 12th–13th century Hoysala sculptor: late-30s, medium-brown complexion, oval face with narrow focused eyes and a small half-smile, thick black hair pulled into a neat low knot at the back of his head, held by a simple off-white cotton headband across his forehead. Show his indigo blue, long-sleeved knee-length tunic with a subtle woven grid texture, worn over a cream-colored ankle-length dhoti with a narrow dark brown border, and a soft light-brown cotton angavastra draped over one shoulder. Include thin gold chain at the neck, small gold stud earrings, off-white cloth wraps on his forearms, a plain fabric belt with small tool loops, and simple leather sandals. Place a long iron chisel with a square shaft and flattened cutting edge in his right hand and a medium wooden mallet in his left, both dusty and worn. Use a palette dominated by indigo blue, cream, light brown, dark brown, and black, and show him front, side, and back to make the costume, hair knot, headband, and tools completely clear.
